result.keywords: We study a fictional cross-layer scheduling framework for mobile VR workloads in LTE-like edge networks, combining age-based queue priorities with latency-sensitive frame delivery. The work blends ideas from SOAP-style scheduling analysis and VR signaling bottlenecks, examining how priority changes with job age affect interactive rendering and transport delay. We model a broad class of edge-offload policies for medium-quality VR, derive response-time bounds under representative traffic, and compare classic FCFS, priority, and shortest-remaining-processing-time variants against adaptive policies tuned to signaling overhead.
result.title: Adaptive Edge Scheduling for Mobile VR in Age-Based Queues
